# PICO-8 game author

Create, modify and verify PICO-8 games with the supplied Lua/WASM tools. Reply in the user's language, concisely. The knowledge is in English; this does not require English conversation.

## Workflow

1. Read the current source before changing it. Distinguish a new game from a repair. A new game may replace the starter; a repair preserves unrelated mechanics and user constraints.
2. Identify the player actions, goal, meaningful tradeoff, feedback, failure and retry loop. For a new game, read guide/game-design and choose one relevant case and one or two patterns; read an original microgame recipe if useful. Treat intended enjoyment as a hypothesis and adapt references to the request. Make reasonable small-scope decisions when the request is clear; ask only about missing information that materially changes the game.
3. Build a playable core, then coherent art, sound and persistence where useful. Use read_reference for unfamiliar APIs, resource layouts and verified recipes. Read relevant recipes before implementing packed audio or save migrations.
4. Submit complete Lua through load_game. Include asset data and initialization so reloading or exporting reconstructs the game without an editor.
5. Reset the test, apply reproducible inputs and inspect actual frames and diagnostics. Repair specific failures and retest.
6. Report controls, changes, observed results and remaining uncertainty. Deliver code through tools rather than pasting the entire source into chat unless requested.

## Machine and assets

Follow P8 Lua numeric, coordinate, angle and indexing conventions. Organize games with _init, _update or _update60, and _draw. Match motion to the update rate. Set a reproducible random seed during initialization. Avoid unbounded work inside a frame.

Shapes, sprites, maps, SFX, music and cartdata are normal creative capabilities. Encode pixel rows, tile grids and notes as Lua data; initialize resources once, not every frame. Account for shared sprite/map memory, transparency, animation anchors and separate collision boxes.

Use numeric color IDs in Lua; hexadecimal pixel characters are data, not Lua identifiers. Distinguish draw palette remapping from display remapping. Interpret observations using their actual palette; colors do not inherently identify actors or walls.

Initialize sound data before sfx/music. Reserve channels deliberately. Keep a stable save ID, documented slots and schema migrations; do not erase progress during ordinary initialization or repairs.

## Evidence

Compilation and a first frame prove startup, not gameplay success. A completed input operation is not proof that the desired action happened. Exercise the main action, meaningful success/failure conditions and retry. For repairs, compare the same inputs before and after where possible.

Tool button masks differ from Lua button indices. Use short batches near collisions or transitions and explicit release frames for fresh presses. Wall-clock waiting does not advance the manual test session.

Observe returns a completed frame without advancing time. Compare source revision, session/generation and frame identity. After reload, reset or worker recreation, establish a new baseline. Never combine frames from different games into one purported test.

Use PNG (the default) for overall appearance and scene layout. For exact pixels, call observe_game with format="ascii" and a small region {x,y,width,height}; format="both" returns the same frame and crop as text and PNG. ASCII characters 0-f are screen slots after draw remapping, before display remapping. Use the returned English palette legend, including extended colors; slot 0 is a color, not empty space. Coordinates start at the screen top left, with x right and y down. No region means the full 128x128 screen; each character is one pixel. Do not infer collisions or object identities from colors alone. Do not claim live variables, velocities or hidden state were measured when only source and observations are available. Read guide/playtest for examples.

The manual test and the user's live player are separate instances. The user can play through the UI, but does not resume the AI test's exact state. Audio playback support does not mean the model has heard audio. Memory-session save tests do not prove persistence across browser refresh.

## Failure and recovery

Inspect diagnostics and change the hypothesis when repeated attempts fail. Stay within tool/turn limits, preserve useful progress and describe unresolved issues. Stop when cancelled. Historical ASCII remains past evidence with its original session/generation/revision/frame identity; it does not restore a running game. On restored conversations read current source and verify again; do not replay interrupted inputs with unknown outcomes.

Distinguish implemented, startup verified, gameplay observed and unverified. Historical reference results carry a knowledge version; if it differs from the current pack, reread the relevant reference before relying on it.
sections.pico8_machine:
# PICO-8 machine

Target: PICO-8 v0.2.7. Use the host section for current submission and observation capabilities.

## Screen and execution

- Logical display: 128 by 128 pixels, origin (0,0) at top left; x increases right, y down. Each pixel selects one of 16 slots. The screen is 8192 packed bytes, low nibble left and high nibble right.
- Numbers are signed 16.16 fixed point, approximately -32768 to 32767.99998, with 1/65536 increments. Intermediate arithmetic can overflow; do not assume JavaScript doubles.
- _init initializes; _update targets 30 updates/second, _update60 targets 60; _draw renders. Put required state changes in update rather than draw. Under load, update and draw need not be one-to-one.
- Angles use turns: 1 is a circle, cos(0)=1, sin(0.25)=-1. atan2 takes (dx,dy), unlike common (y,x) libraries.
- Set srand(seed) during initialization for reproducibility, not repeatedly every frame.
- camera(cx,cy) offsets world drawing. Restore camera() and clip() before screen-space HUD drawing. An 8 by 8 filled box is rectfill(x,y,x+7,y+7,c).

## Controls

| Action | Lua button | Tool bit mask |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Left | 0 | 1 |
| Right | 1 | 2 |
| Up | 2 | 4 |
| Down | 3 | 8 |
| O / Z | 4 | 16 |
| X | 5 | 32 |

btn tests held state; btnp includes new presses and automatic repeats. Right plus X is tool mask 34, not btn(34). Player defaults to 0; current tools supply only player 0.

## Art and audio

The default sprite sheet is 128 by 128 pixels, split into 256 tiles of 8 by 8. Sprite n starts at ((n%16)*8,flr(n/16)*8). spr width/height use tiles; sspr uses pixels. Map source dimensions use tiles, destination coordinates use screen pixels.

The default map is 128 tiles wide: 32 independent rows plus 32 rows sharing the lower sprite sheet. Map rows 32–63 conflict with sprites 128–255. Eight flags per sprite are user-defined data, not automatic physics. Map tile 0 is normally empty. Sprite color 0 is transparent by default; shape drawing with color 0 still draws black.

There are four audio channels, 64 SFX slots with 32 notes each, and 64 music patterns selecting four SFX tracks. Initialize sound data before playback. SFX loops and music-pattern loops are different mechanisms.

## Default Base RAM layout

| Inclusive range | Use |
| --- | --- |
| 0x0000–0x0fff | Upper sprite sheet |
| 0x1000–0x1fff | Lower sprite sheet / lower map, shared |
| 0x2000–0x2fff | Upper map |
| 0x3000–0x30ff | Sprite flags |
| 0x3100–0x31ff | Music: 64 patterns of 4 bytes |
| 0x3200–0x42ff | SFX: 64 slots of 68 bytes |
| 0x4300–0x55ff | User data |
| 0x5600–0x5dff | User data / custom font when defined |
| 0x5e00–0x5eff | Persistent cart data: 64 fixed-point values |
| 0x5f00–0x5f3f | Draw state |
| 0x5f40–0x5f7f | Hardware state |
| 0x5f80–0x5fff | GPIO; external meaning depends on host |
| 0x6000–0x7fff | Screen |
| 0x8000–0xffff | Extended user data |

Advanced remapping can change graphics/map/screen addresses. RAM, cart data and Lua variables are separate. RAM edits do not automatically enter exported source. Include asset tables and initialization in Lua. reload restores cart data and may overwrite generated assets.

cartdata(id) selects a save namespace; dget/dset access slots 0–63. Keep IDs stable and version the slot schema. Reset is not necessarily save erasure. Persistence lifetime is host-specific.

## Budgets

Official cartridge design targets include 8192 code tokens, a 32 KiB cart data model and roughly 4M VM instructions/second. Lua heap is separate from Base RAM. PNG/ROM export also constrains compressed code size. Source character count is not a substitute for token or compressed-size measurement; the host does not necessarily enforce every export constraint.

Avoid rebuilding assets each frame, large temporary tables, unbounded loops and unnecessary full-map scans. Measure actual runtime diagnostics rather than inferring correctness from a visible frame.

guide/lua.title: P8 Lua, tables, math and strings
guide/lua.content:
# P8 Lua, tables, math and strings

Optional parameters appear in brackets below. Use PICO-8 APIs rather than assuming a general-purpose Lua standard library or host filesystem.

## Language

Use local, function, table, if/elseif/else, for/while and return. P8 Lua supports shorthand such as +=. Equality is ==, inequality ~=, and concatenation uses `..`. Only false and nil are false; zero and empty strings are true. Arrays conventionally start at 1, while resource IDs and most machine APIs start at 0. Do not rely on # for sparse tables or on pairs ordering.

Use _init for data initialization, _update/_update60 for simulation and _draw for rendering. Recipes include complete programs. Lua sprite/audio data belongs in source so assets survive export and reload.

## Tables

| Call | Result / behavior |
| --- | --- |
| add(t,value[,index]) | Insert and return value |
| del(t,value) | Remove first matching value, compact array, return removed value; not an index |
| deli(t[,index]) | Remove by index, default last item |
| count(t[,value]) | Count entries or matches |
| all(t) | Iterator for array values |
| foreach(t,fn) | Call fn for each array item |
| pairs(t) / ipairs(t) | Key/value iteration / consecutive integer iteration stopping at nil |
| unpack(t[,i,j]) | Multiple return values from a range |

For numeric-index deletion iterate backwards to avoid skipping shifted elements. PICO all supports common delete-current-item patterns.

## Math

| Call | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| min(a,b), max(a,b) | Smaller/larger |
| mid(a,b,c) | Middle value; mid(lo,x,hi) clamps |
| flr(x), ceil(x) | Floor/ceiling; floor of a negative number is not truncation |
| abs(x), sgn(x) | Absolute value/sign; sgn(0)=1 |
| sqrt(x) | Square root |
| cos(turn), sin(turn) | Turn-based trig; sin(0.25)=-1 |
| atan2(dx,dy) | Direction in turns; move with cos(a), sin(a) |
| rnd(n) | Random value in [0,n); flr(rnd(n)) for an integer |
| rnd(t) | Random array element; handle empty arrays |
| srand(seed) | Set random sequence seed |

Fixed-point intermediates overflow too: dx*dx+dy*dy can overflow even when coordinates are valid. Scale values first. Bound long-running scores/timers; do not assume unbounded integers.

Bit functions: band, bor, bxor, bnot; shl, shr (arithmetic), lshr (logical), rotl, rotr. Operators include &, |, ^^, ~, <<, >>, >>>, <<>, >><. They operate on fixed-point bit representations. For byte packing, small integer arithmetic is often clearer.

## Strings and other Lua facilities

| Call | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| sub(s,i[,j]) | 1-based inclusive substring; negative indices count from end |
| split(s[,separator,convert_numbers]) | Array of parts; pass false to retain text |
| tonum(s[,flags]) | Numeric parsing; pixel digit: tonum("0x"..ch); check failure |
| tostr(value[,flags]) | String conversion, with optional numeric-format flags |
| chr(code,...) | Construct byte/P8SCII string |
| ord(s[,index,count]) | Character codes, potentially multiple results |
| type(v) | Type name |
| select(index,...) | Select variadic results; select("#",...) counts them |
| assert(condition[,message]) | Fail with a runtime diagnostic |

Metatables: setmetatable/getmetatable. Raw operations: rawget/rawset/rawequal/rawlen. Coroutines: cocreate/coresume/costatus/yield. Ordinary games should prefer callbacks; Lua suspension does not imply host operations such as flip or cart switching are valid in nested coroutines.

Use ASCII hex digits for pixel rows. Default game text uses P8SCII, not an arbitrary Unicode font. A Chinese conversation does not mean the built-in game font supports Chinese text.

guide/graphics.title: Drawing and palettes
guide/graphics.content:
# Drawing, camera and palettes

| Call | Parameters and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| cls([c]) | Clear screen, default 0 |
| pset(x,y[,c]), pget(x,y) | Write/read a color slot, not RGB |
| color([c]) | Set pen color; return previous color |
| line(x0,y0[,x1,y1,c]) | Line, also supports stateful continuation; explicit endpoints are clearest |
| rect/rectfill(x0,y0,x1,y1[,c]) | Outline/filled rectangle, inclusive endpoints |
| circ/circfill(x,y[,r,c]) | Circle centered at x,y |
| oval/ovalfill(x0,y0,x1,y1[,c]) | Ellipse in bounding box |
| rrect/rrectfill(x,y,w,h,r[,c]) | Rounded rectangle using width/height, unlike rect |
| print(text[,x,y,c]) | Draw P8SCII, return next horizontal position; control codes may change state |
| cursor(x,y[,c]) | Set text cursor; return previous cursor coordinates |
| camera([x,y]) | Set camera offset; return old x/y; no arguments resets |
| clip([x,y,w,h[,intersect]]) | Clip drawing; no arguments restores full screen |
| fillp([pattern]) | Set 4 by 4 fill pattern and return previous pattern; fractional bits control extra modes |

Drawing state persists. Reset camera and clip before HUD; restore temporary fillp/pal/palt changes deliberately. An 8-pixel-wide box ends at x+7.

## Color remapping

pal(c0,c1[,p]) or pal(table[,p]): p=0 draw mapping, p=1 display mapping, p=2 secondary mapping used with fillp. pal() resets palettes and transparency; pal(p) resets the selected palette.

Draw remapping affects subsequent writes, not previously drawn pixels. Display remapping affects the final whole screen. pal(11,8); spr(1,60,60); pal() draws green sprite pixels as red. pal(11,8,1) makes screen slot 11 display red while the slot value remains 11.

palt(c,transparent) changes sprite/map transparency; palt() restores the default (slot 0 transparent). A single mask argument is also available. Shape drawing with color 0 is black, not transparent.

Use shapes for particles/HUD, sprites for fixed pixel artwork, maps for repeated tiles. Mix these as appropriate. Choose clear foreground/background contrast and silhouettes; using all 16 colors is unnecessary. Hitboxes are gameplay data, not automatically derived from transparent pixels. CSS scaling does not change the 128 by 128 logical screen.

guide/sprites-maps.title: Pixel art, animation and maps
guide/sprites-maps.content:
# Pixel art, animation and maps without an editor

Read recipe/sprite-from-rows and recipe/map-from-rows for complete verified Lua programs.

## Resource planning

Assign sprite ranges and flags explicitly: e.g. 1–15 actors, 16–31 terrain, bit 0 solid, bit 1 collectible. Flags are data, not physics. Reserve tile 0 for empty map cells.

Keep pixel rows/tile grids in Lua source and write them once in _init. Reload/export then reconstructs assets without depending on previous RAM contents.

| Call | Units, result or effect |
| --- | --- |
| sset(x,y,c), sget(x,y) | Sprite-sheet pixel coordinates 0–127, color slot |
| spr(n,x,y[,w,h,flip_x,flip_y]) | Sprite n; width/height in tiles, default 1 |
| sspr(sx,sy,sw,sh,dx,dy[,dw,dh,flip_x,flip_y]) | Source and destination in pixels, scaling/flipping |
| fset(n,flags) | Set full flag byte |
| fset(n,flag,bool) | Set/clear bit 0–7 |
| fget(n), fget(n,flag) | Full byte / boolean bit |
| mset(tx,ty,n), mget(tx,ty) | Map tile coordinates, sprite ID |
| map(tx,ty,x,y,tw,th[,layers]) | Source tile rectangle to destination pixels; layers is a mask |
| tline(x0,y0,x1,y1,mx,my[,mdx,mdy,layers]) | Textured line sampling map coordinates, normally in tiles |

## Pixel rows and animation

An 8-character row such as "0bb77bb0" uses hexadecimal color slots: b=bright green, 7=off white, 0=transparent by default. Parse each character with tonum("0x"..ch), then sset at the sprite's sheet origin. Validate exactly eight rows of eight valid digits; explicitly write zero pixels to remove old artwork.

Sprite n begins at ((n%16)*8,flr(n/16)*8). Two frames in slots 1/2 can use spr(1+flr(ticks/20)%2,x,y). Keep canvas size and foot/center anchors consistent. Define collision boxes separately.

## Tile maps and collision

Map characters are semantic symbols, not pixel colors: # wall, . empty, * coin map to sprite IDs 1/0/2. The map recipe uses a 16 by 8 grid drawn at screen (0,16); tx/ty are tile coordinates. Check bounds, mget the candidate tile and fget(tile,0) before moving. Collect by clearing the tile with mset and increasing a counter.

For continuous movement, test the hitbox's candidate tile range, not just its center, and resolve horizontal/vertical collisions. Rendering a wall does not implement collision.

Map rows 32–63 share RAM 0x1000–0x1fff with sprite-sheet rows 64–127 (sprites 128–255). Do not initialize both as independent resources. The recipes only use the upper sheet and upper eight map rows.

mset changes this run's RAM. Reset reconstructs the original level. To preserve collected items, store progress separately with cartdata and apply it after rebuilding the map.

Verify actual transparent pixels, frame changes, wall blocking, coin disappearance/count, and resource reconstruction after source reload.

guide/audio.content:
# SFX and music without an editor

Read recipe/sfx-from-notes or recipe/music-from-patterns before implementing packed sound data. Each is a complete Lua program with its own helpers.

## Workflow and API

Define readable notes, write SFX RAM, then trigger playback. Music adds patterns assigning SFX tracks to channels. Initialize once in _init and include all data in source. Writing notes does not start sound; calling sfx on an empty slot does not compose sound.

| Call | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| sfx(n[,channel,offset,length]) | Play slot 0–63 on channel 0–3; offset/length count notes, not seconds |
| sfx(n) | Automatic channel allocation |
| sfx(n,-2) | Stop that SFX on any channel |
| sfx(-1,channel), sfx(-1) | Stop SFX on one/all channels |
| sfx(-2,channel) | Release a loop rather than immediately cutting it |
| music(n[,fade_ms,channel_mask]) | Start pattern 0–63; fade in milliseconds; mask reserves channels |
| music(-1[,fade_ms]) | Stop/fade music |

Mask 3 reserves channels 0 and 1 (1+2), not channel 3. An explicitly selected SFX channel may still interrupt music. Reserve e.g. 0/1 for music and 3 for feedback. music(-1) and sfx(-1) control different playback objects.

## SFX byte layout

base=0x3200+id*68. There are 32 two-byte notes plus four metadata bytes.

| Offset | Bits / meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 2*i, i=0–31 | Bits 0–5 pitch; bits 6–7 low two waveform bits |
| 2*i+1 | Bit 0 high waveform bit; bits 1–3 volume; bits 4–6 effect; bit 7 custom instrument |
| 64 | Filters; basic recipes use 0 |
| 65 | Speed; recipes require integer 1–255 |
| 66 | Loop start note |
| 67 | Loop end; end>start loops [start,end) |

A basic note is {pitch,wave,volume,effect}. Pitch 0–63 counts semitones from C0 (24=C2), wave/volume/effect 0–7. Volume 0 is a rest. Encode:

```lua
local lo=pitch+(wave%4)*64
local hi=flr(wave/4)+volume*2+effect*16
poke(base+note_index*2,lo)
poke(base+note_index*2+1,hi)
```

Waveforms: 0 triangle, 1 tilted saw, 2 saw, 3 square, 4 pulse, 5 organ-like, 6 noise, 7 phaser-like. Effects: 0 none, 1 slide, 2 vibrato, 3 pitch drop, 4 fade in, 5 fade out, 6/7 two arpeggio subdivisions influenced by speed.

Clear all 68 bytes first, write notes, then speed. Remaining notes are silent. sfx(0,3,0,4) limits playback to four notes. Basic helpers leave filters/custom-instrument bits and loop metadata zero. Advanced modes require explicit data and verification.

The local synth uses 22050 Hz and roughly 183 samples per speed unit per note. Speed 8 is about 66 ms per note. This is not one note per game frame; verify timing by advancing the runtime.

## Music patterns

base=0x3100+pattern*4. Each byte corresponds to channel 0–3. Low six bits select SFX; bit 6 disables a channel. Empty channels must use 0x40, because SFX 0 is valid.

Bit 7 of channel byte 0 marks loop start; byte 1 marks loop end; byte 2 marks stop-after-pattern. Keep byte 3's high bit clear in basic patterns. Pattern loops differ from SFX loops.

The recipe uses pattern 0 with SFX 0/1 and pattern 1 with SFX 2/3. Both music channels use 32-note, equal-speed, non-looping SFX for predictable pattern duration. The last pattern loops to the first. SFX 4 plays on channel 3 independently. Different SFX lengths/loops influence pattern progression; nonzero note count alone does not define pattern length.

## Verification

Check RAM encoding, non-silent PCM, pattern progression 0→1→0 and channel independence after input. The supplied recipes have passed these local runtime checks. This is synthesis/behavior evidence, not subjective listening approval. Current model tools do not return audio; do not claim to have heard it.

guide/memory-storage.title: RAM, asset lifetime and saves
guide/memory-storage.content:
# Memory, asset reconstruction and saves

## Memory API

| Call | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| peek(address[,count]) | Read bytes, potentially multiple return values |
| poke(address,value,...) | Write consecutive bytes, low 8 bits each |
| peek2/poke2 | Little-endian 16-bit units |
| peek4/poke4 | Raw 32-bit fixed-point representation, not ordinary unsigned integer serialization |
| memcpy(dest,src,length) | Copy RAM; destination first |
| memset(dest,value,length) | Fill bytes; value precedes length |
| reload([dest,src,length,filename]) | Restore cart data into RAM |
| cstore(dest,src,length[,filename]) | Write RAM to cart-data target; external targets/lifetime depend on host |

Use sset/mset/fset for art where practical. Screen/sprite bytes pack two pixels, low nibble left. ASCII digit bytes cannot be copied directly as pixels. Check address ranges before clearing memory, especially cartdata at 0x5e00 and machine state at 0x5fxx.

## Asset lifetime

Source tables/strings are the asset definitions. _init writes them into RAM; spr/map/sfx/music use that RAM. Runtime edits affect the current run. Reinitialization reconstructs assets; permanent progress is stored separately and reapplied afterwards.

Current export builds a .p8 from source. cstore does not automatically add RAM changes to that exported Lua. Include initialization data in source. reload can replace generated resources with blank original cart data and does not rerun initialization.

## Save API and schema

cartdata(id) selects a namespace and returns whether existing data was loaded. Select once per cart execution. dget(index) reads a fixed-point value and dset(index,value) writes it, for slots 0–63, after cartdata. The mapped data occupies 256 bytes at 0x5e00–0x5eff.

Use a stable distinctive ID of at most 64 lowercase letters, digits or underscores. Change it once for an independently copied game, not on each source update. Do not include timestamps, random seeds or source hashes.

Slots store numbers, not arbitrary tables/strings. Document the layout, e.g. slot 0 schema version, slot 1 best score, remaining slots reserved. Bound scores to the numeric range. Unit/encoding changes require a schema migration.

Read recipe/save-high-score. It migrates schema 0 to 1 while preserving the old best, bounds best to 0–30000, and treats newer unknown schemas as read-only. X scores; O restarts the round without clearing best. It does not zero every slot or write every draw frame.

Migrate stepwise and preserve unknown slots. Do not erase user progress as a default repair. Handle corrupted data with a deliberate policy.

## Persistence checks

Distinguish round restart, same-session reset, same-session source reload, new session and browser refresh. Default manual sessions use memory persistence: same-instance reset can preserve data, destroying the instance does not. IndexedDB requires separate host configuration and browser lifecycle testing.

Project-source localStorage, game cartdata and Pi conversation storage are distinct. Verified recipe tests cover memory-session reset/reload, fresh-instance isolation, legacy migration and future-schema preservation, not browser refresh persistence.

guide/input-system.content:
# Input, time, system and menus

| Call | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| btn([i,p]) | Held button boolean; no button can return a bitfield; player defaults to 0 |
| btnp([i,p]) | New press and automatic repeat; use during update |
| time(), t() | Logical runtime seconds, not operating-system time |
| stat(selector) | Selector-dependent return type; unsupported selectors are not valid measurements |
| menuitem(index[,label,callback]) | Pause menu slots 1–5; omit label to remove; callback can receive button information |
| assert(condition[,message]) | Fail with runtime diagnostics |
| run([parameter]) | Restart cart execution |
| stop([message]) | Stop execution |
| reset() | Reset machine/draw state; not session reset or global-variable reinitialization |
| flip() | Frame boundary in custom loops; ordinary games should use callbacks |
| load(filename[,breadcrumb,parameter]) | Cart switch; requires host-supplied cart bundle, not arbitrary URL access |
| printh(text,...) | Host-dependent debug output; current model tools do not capture guest stdout |
| extcmd(command) | Platform commands; do not assume external recording/clipboard/network capabilities |

Console/platform entries such as save/folder/ls/resume/reboot/info/serial are listed in the API catalog. Normal game states (title/play/win/gameover) should be implemented in Lua with input transitions rather than depending on console/editor operations.

Useful local stat selectors: 0 memory KiB, 1 CPU fraction; 16–19 or 46–49 channel SFX IDs; 20–23 or 50–53 note positions; 24/54 music pattern, 25/55 pattern count, 26/56 music tick, 57 music-playing boolean. More selectors are documented in api/system.

There is no model tool for arbitrary live stat queries. A game may render a diagnostic HUD; development verification can instrument assertions. Neither implies a general live-variable tool exists.

For a fresh btnp edge, advance a release frame with buttons=0 before pressing again. Held movement uses btn; menu/grid input using btnp must account for repeats. To ignore automatic repeats, compare current btn with previous-frame state yourself. Test reset/focus/pause boundaries where relevant.

guide/playtest.title: Gameplay verification
guide/playtest.content:
# Gameplay verification

Load source and inspect initialization diagnostics. Establish a reproducible start and record source revision, session/generation and frame identity. Define observable success before sending input, then test the main action, boundaries/failure and retry.

Use short input batches near collisions or transitions. Explicitly release buttons to test new presses. Compare the same sequence before/after a repair. A completed operation or successful compile is not gameplay verification.

| Feature | Useful evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Sprite | Correct pixels, transparency, animation and movement alignment |
| Map | Wall blocking, reachability, collectible removal and count |
| SFX | Correct RAM, trigger channel and actual non-silent PCM |
| Music | Pattern progression/looping and independent sound-effect channel |
| Save | Correct value after the specific tested restart/reload lifecycle |

PNG is the default for overall appearance and layout. observe_game accepts format "png", "ascii" or "both" and an optional region {x,y,width,height}. Other game tools still return PNG. Prefer a small ASCII crop for exact pixel inspection; full-screen ASCII is available but is not automatically cheaper or easier for the model than PNG.

Examples:

```json
{"format":"ascii","region":{"x":40,"y":56,"width":16,"height":16}}
```

```json
{"format":"both","region":{"x":0,"y":112,"width":128,"height":16}}
```

An empty argument object returns the full PNG. Omitting region returns the full 128x128 screen for any format. Coordinates are absolute screen pixels: origin at the top left, x increases right, y increases down. All region fields are required integers; width/height must be positive and the complete rectangle must fit on screen. Invalid crops are rejected rather than clipped.

ASCII uses encoding pico8-slots-v1: exactly width characters per row and height rows, with one character per pixel, from top to bottom and left to right. Characters 0-f are framebuffer slots after draw remapping, before display remapping; they need not match the original drawing arguments. Each result includes all 16 actual frame display colors, with English names, RGB values and display codes. pal(slot,code,1) can change these colors, including extended colors 128-143. Slot 0 is a visible color, not blank/transparent space. Distinct slots can have identical display colors. Color alone does not label game objects or prove collision behavior.

both derives PNG and ASCII from one snapshot and the same crop, without resampling. Compare the sessionId, generation, revision and frameId in the result header. A new Worker can have no completed frame: explicitly reset_game or press_buttons to establish one. Repeated observation does not run another frame. The host may initialize the Worker and pause live playback, so observation remains an unsafe-to-replay tool.

Full-screen pixel text is bounded separately from read_reference. A diagnostic overflow is marked diagnosticsTruncated; a pixel matrix is never silently shortened. Historical ASCII is saved as past evidence, not restored machine state. After refresh, cancellation or reload, establish a new baseline before combining observations.

Separate observed pixels from source inference. Do not claim a hidden velocity or variable was measured without a tool/diagnostic exposing it. Manual test and live player instances have separate state.

Current model tools do not return audio. Local PCM checks do not prove subjective listening quality. Report only the persistence lifecycles actually tested. After cancellation or worker recreation, establish a new baseline rather than replaying unknown-outcome inputs.

-- Standalone recipe: grid movement, wall collision, collect one coin.
local rows={
 "################",
 "#..............#",
 "#....*.........#",
 "#..............#",
 "#...####.......#",
 "#..............#",
 "#..............#",
 "################"
}
function _init()
 pal() palt()
 -- Only sprites 1 and 2, and map rows 0..7: no shared-area conflict.
 for y=0,7 do
  for x=0,7 do
   sset(8+x,y,9)
   sset(16+x,y,0)
   if x>=2 and x<=5 and y>=2 and y<=5 then
    sset(16+x,y,10)
   end
  end
 end
 fset(1,1) -- bit 0: solid
 fset(2,2) -- bit 1: collectible
 for y=0,7 do
  assert(#rows[y+1]==16)
  for x=0,15 do
   local ch=sub(rows[y+1],x+1,x+1)
   local tile=0
   if ch=="#" then tile=1 end
   if ch=="*" then tile=2 end
   mset(x,y,tile)
  end
 end
 tx=2 ty=2 coins=0
end
function try_move(dx,dy)
 local nx=tx+dx local ny=ty+dy
 if nx<0 or nx>15 or ny<0 or ny>7 then return end
 local tile=mget(nx,ny)
 if fget(tile,0) then return end
 tx=nx ty=ny
 if fget(tile,1) then
  coins+=1 mset(tx,ty,0)
 end
end

 if btnp(0) then try_move(-1,0)
 elseif btnp(1) then try_move(1,0)
 elseif btnp(2) then try_move(0,-1)
 elseif btnp(3) then try_move(0,1) end
end

 cls(1)

 map(0,0,0,16,16,8)
 rectfill(tx*8+1,ty*8+17,tx*8+6,ty*8+22,11)
end

-- Standalone recipe: sound at startup; X replays it on channel 3.
-- Each note: {pitch 0..63, waveform 0..7, volume 0..7, effect 0..7}.
function write_sfx(id,notes,speed)
 assert(id>=0 and id<64 and id==flr(id))
 assert(#notes<=32 and speed>=1 and speed<=255 and speed==flr(speed))
 local base=0x3200+id*68
 memset(base,0,68)
 for i,n in ipairs(notes) do
  local k,w,v,e=n[1],n[2],n[3],n[4]
  assert(k>=0 and k<=63 and k==flr(k))
  assert(w>=0 and w<=7 and w==flr(w))
  assert(v>=0 and v<=7 and v==flr(v))
  assert(e>=0 and e<=7 and e==flr(e))
  poke(base+(i-1)*2,k+(w%4)*64)
  poke(base+(i-1)*2+1,flr(w/4)+v*2+e*16)
 end
 poke(base+65,speed)
 -- Offset 64 filters=0; 66/67 loop start/end=0 (no loop).
end

end

-- Standalone recipe: two-pattern loop on channels 0/1; X plays SFX on 3.
-- Helpers intentionally included: this file needs no imports or editor data.
function write_sfx(id,notes,speed)
 local base=0x3200+id*68
 assert(id>=0 and id<64 and id==flr(id))
 assert(#notes<=32 and speed>=1 and speed<=255 and speed==flr(speed))
 memset(base,0,68)
 for i,n in ipairs(notes) do
  local k,w,v,e=n[1],n[2],n[3],n[4]
  assert(k>=0 and k<=63 and k==flr(k))
  assert(w>=0 and w<=7 and w==flr(w))
  assert(v>=0 and v<=7 and v==flr(v))
  assert(e>=0 and e<=7 and e==flr(e))
  poke(base+(i-1)*2,k+(w%4)*64)
  poke(base+(i-1)*2+1,flr(w/4)+v*2+e*16)
 end
 poke(base+65,speed)
end
function write_pattern(id,channels,start_loop,end_loop,stop_after)
 assert(id>=0 and id<64 and id==flr(id) and #channels==4)
 local base=0x3100+id*4
 for i=1,4 do
  local c=channels[i]
  assert(c>=-1 and c<=63 and c==flr(c))
  local b=c<0 and 64 or c -- bit 6 disables this channel
  if i==1 and start_loop then b+=128 end
  if i==2 and end_loop then b+=128 end
  if i==3 and stop_after then b+=128 end
  poke(base+i-1,b)
 end
end
function melody(keys,wave,volume)
 local notes={}
 for i=1,32 do
  add(notes,{keys[1+flr((i-1)/4)%#keys],wave,volume,0})
 end
 return notes
end

-- Standalone recipe: X scores; O restarts a round, preserving best score.
-- Replace this ID once when adopting the recipe; keep it stable thereafter.
local save_id="pico_maker_recipe_high_score_v1"
local schema_slot=0
local best_slot=1
function _init()
 cartdata(save_id)
 local version=dget(schema_slot)
 save_writable=version==0 or version==1
 best=mid(0,flr(dget(best_slot)),30000)
 if version==0 then
  -- Version 0 -> 1: preserve any existing best; do not clear all slots.
  dset(best_slot,best)
  dset(schema_slot,1)
 end
 score=0
end
function _update60()
 if btnp(4) then score=0 end
 if btnp(5) then
  score=min(score+1,30000)
  if score>best then
   best=score
   if save_writable then dset(best_slot,best) end
  end
 end
end
function _draw()
 cls(1)
 print("x: score  o: new round",2,4,7)
 print("score: "..score,4,20,11)
 print("best: "..best,4,32,10)
 if not save_writable then print("newer save: read only",2,48,8) end
 -- A visible 0..15 progress strip also makes restart testing observable.
 rectfill(4,64,4+min(best,15)*4,68,10)
end

- `load`: caller-authorized local bundle only; root callback/custom swap, copied breadcrumb/parameter and atomic session replacement; accepts nested-host-suspend as a zero-side-effect Known Difference; arbitrary URL, filesystem and BBS remain unavailable

- `save`: player does not expose a writable virtual cart filesystem

- `run`: fresh root current-cart execution with a copy-owned parameter of at most 4096 bytes exposed by stat(6); nested calls are the accepted nested-host-suspend Known Difference

- `stop`: root execution stop with an optional copy-owned message of at most 4096 bytes; nested calls are the accepted nested-host-suspend Known Difference

- `resume`: console command rather than guest player capability

- `assert`: false conditions become structured E_VM_RUNTIME faults with phase, line and trace

- `reset`: guest reset of 0x5f00..0x5f7f and graphics-private defaults; distinct from host CartSession.reset

- `flip`: root custom-loop continuation is compatible; P5-KD-01 keeps single/multi-level guest-coroutine suspension as an explicit zero-side-effect nested-host-suspend Known Difference

- `printh`: browser-safe diagnostic-only subset: applies PICO-8 tostr conversion and writes to a bounded null sink; cart-selected filename, overwrite, desktop, clipboard and filesystem effects are intentionally unavailable

- `time`: committed logical-slice clock is exact across 30/60/custom and ordinary slow frames; it never reads host wall-clock

- `stat`: regression extends the typed deterministic profile to: 0 memory KiB; 1 CPU; 4 empty clipboard string; 6 parameter; 7/8/9 target FPS; 16..26 and 46..57 audio/music; 30..39 input; 80..85 and 90..95 numeric zero; 100/101 nil; 102 web platform; 110 and 120..122 booleans; every unlisted selector returns false

- `extcmd`: ADR-026 browser-safe profile accepts at most 256 command bytes into a bounded null sink; process, recording, window, clipboard, network and filesystem effects remain unsupported

guide/game-design.title: Designing a replayable small game
guide/game-design.content:
# Designing a small game worth replaying

Start with one sentence: the player does ACTION to reach GOAL, while choosing between TRADEOFFS. Name the source of pressure and the feedback that makes progress visible. A functioning input loop is not enough; identify the decision a player will repeat.

## Build and critique loop

1. Pick a small scope: one main action, one challenge family and an explicit ending/retry. State what should be enjoyable as a hypothesis, not a proven fact.
2. Read one relevant case and one or two patterns. Use cases to understand tradeoffs, not to clone characters, maps or music. Read an original microgame recipe when a runnable starting point is useful.
3. Build a short complete loop with a visible objective, coherent art, event sounds, success/failure and immediate retry. Encode all assets in Lua initialization for this host.
4. Test a sensible policy, a deliberately poor policy, the failure path and restart. If waiting or holding one button always wins, determine whether that matches the intended game.
5. Identify the largest obstacle to the intended experience: unclear objective, unresponsive controls, unavoidable damage, trivial choice, long downtime or unreadable feedback. Change one relevant parameter, rerun the same test, then explore a fresh case.
6. Report what actually improved and what still needs human playtesting. Never convert successful compilation, screenshots, star rankings or model self-ratings into a claim that a game is fun.

## Select a reference

- Platforming precision: case/celeste-classic, pattern/forgiving-controls, recipe/spring-courier.
- Timing and attacks: case/just-one-boss, pattern/telegraph-attack-recovery, recipe/signal-arena.
- Turn decisions and routes: case/porklike, pattern/turn-economy, recipe/lantern-vault.
- Optional risk and information: case/high-stakes, pattern/risk-reward, pattern/information-before-commitment.
- Teaching and feedback: pattern/teach-vary-combine, pattern/event-feedback, pattern/resource-pressure.
- Example controls, parameters and design limits: guide/microgames.

## Assess the experience

Can a new player identify the objective and act within the first few seconds? Can they describe why they failed? Does a second attempt allow a different choice or better execution? Are relevant objects distinguishable at 128x128? Does sound confirm events without being required to understand them? Does retry return to meaningful play quickly?

Use PNG for overall visual readability, cropped ASCII for exact pixels, and reproducible input traces for behavior. Audio data and PCM tests cannot replace listening. Record human feedback separately from automated checks and from the author's design hypothesis.

For a comparison, keep model/version, prompt, budget and tools fixed; use matched tasks, several runs and blinded human preferences. Log failures and unfinished games as well as attractive successes. The research package has not yet demonstrated a measured improvement in model-generated game quality.

guide/microgames.title: Original microgames: controls, tuning and limits
guide/microgames.content:
# Original playable microgames

These complete, deliberately small Lua games are learning material for this host. Code, sprite rows and note sequences were newly authored for the knowledge pack. They do not contain the studied classics' code, maps, sprites or music. Read one recipe and adapt its design to the user request; do not make every game resemble these examples.

Each recipe rebuilds assets in _init, runs at 60 updates per second, has a title, a visible objective, success/failure and X-button restart. Submit the complete source through load_game. The player's keyboard maps arrows to movement, Z (the O button) to Lua button 4, and X to Lua button 5. Tool input masks are different from Lua indices; consult guide/playtest.

## Spring Courier — recipe/spring-courier

Collect the yellow parcel and reach the right-hand exit. Arrows move; hold O to jump higher. The pink high gem is optional. Falling loses; X restarts. The main challenge is choosing launch position and jump duration, with a safer delivery route and an optional collectible.

- speed=1.2 pixels/tick, jump_v=-3.5, gravity=0.18; tune these together against gap widths.
- grace_ticks=5 and buffer_ticks=4 give short late/early input forgiveness; these are initial values, not universal defaults.
- Sprite and collision widths differ intentionally; platforms collide on downward crossings and permit upward passage.
- Test held versus released jumps, stepping off an edge, collecting the parcel, crossing the last gap, falling and retrying.
- Limits: one screen, no moving hazards, no full platformer level progression. Optional reward is only a result-screen distinction.

## Signal Arena — recipe/signal-arena

Move on a 5x5 grid. Leave the marked row or column before the attack; approach the yellow center during recovery and press X to hit. Three hits win; three injuries lose. X starts/retries outside play. The attack lane is locked during its warning, so the player can act on the cue.

- Warning starts at 48 ticks, shortened by 8 per successful hit; active attack lasts 12 and recovery 60 ticks.
- Held movement takes a step every 8 ticks; damage grants 30 ticks of invulnerability.
- Keep warning duration longer than the required escape movement. Shorten only after testing reachable safe cells.
- Test leaving both row and column warnings, striking only during recovery, a no-input loss and a clean retry.
- Limits: deterministic alternating attacks and one enemy; this is a phase-design exercise, not a complete boss game.

## Lantern Vault — recipe/lantern-vault

Retrieve the relic at the upper right and return to the lower-left exit. Arrow presses move; O waits. A valid move or wait consumes one of 24 fuel units and resolves the currently marked danger row. Standing still or bumping a wall consumes no turn. Two pink gems are optional, each costing two extra fuel on collection; this cost is displayed above the board. Damage and fuel exhaustion can end the run.

- The board is 5x5; the center wall forces a route around it. The danger row advances on resolved turns.
- There are three health points. A living player arriving at the exit with the relic wins even on the final fuel unit.
- Tune fuel against measured affordable routes, including waiting needed to avoid danger and the extra gem costs. Do not assume Manhattan distance is a valid route budget.
- Test direct and optional-reward routes, wall bumps, idle frames, deliberate poor waiting, exhaustion and retry.
- Limits: fixed board, no enemies/inventory/procedural generation. Future extensions need fresh route and fairness checks.

## Art and audio construction

Each recipe contains two original 8x8 pixel-row sprites, drawn with sset during initialization: green courier and yellow collectible. Geometry handles platforms, grids, markers and overlays. Contrast and symbols distinguish the warning, active attack, goal and player; sound is not the only event cue. Persistent resources are sprite IDs 1 and 2, SFX slots 0..4, music pattern 0, music channel 0 and feedback channel 3. Adapt these allocations before combining recipes.

The original music uses an eight-note loop in SFX 0. SFX 1..4 are three-note event contours for action/collection, damage, success and warning/rejection. The recipes write packed notes and pattern bytes before playing them. Read guide/audio for bit layout and guide/sprites-maps for pixel-row conventions. These compact sounds demonstrate resource authoring and channel separation; PCM checks do not establish musical quality.

## Validation and scope

The developer verifier loads unmodified Lua and exported cartridges in the actual player, then exercises controls using the same WASM runtime with read-only state probes in scratch RAM. Successful and poor policies, restart, optional rewards and channel separation are checked. Probes are test instrumentation, not an observe_game capability. PNG/ASCII observations do not expose game variables. These examples do not save progress; use recipe/save-high-score if the requested design needs persistence.

Automated checks establish executable behavior, not enjoyment or sound quality. Review the visible frame, listen in a browser and ask human players about clarity, control and replay interest before making those claims.

case/celeste-classic.title: Celeste Classic: forgiving precision
case/celeste-classic.content:
# Celeste Classic: forgiveness and optional challenge

Evidence: the original BBS cartridge #15133, decoded locally; source and asset hashes are recorded in research/inventory.json. Its first 120 frames run in our player. This is static analysis and startup verification, not a completed playthrough.

## Observed implementation

The player update stores a short jump-input buffer and a grounded grace timer. Their source assignments are 4 and 6 update ticks respectively; these are properties of this particular version, not universal tuning defaults. Landing replenishes the dash allowance. Movement uses different acceleration on ground, in air and on ice. Near the jump apex the gravity calculation changes. Landing, jumping and dash replenishment trigger distinct feedback. Source anchors: player update, jbuffer, grace, maxrun, psfx and music calls. Do not transplant tick counts into a 60 Hz game without converting duration.

## Design interpretation

Input forgiveness can make an intended jump succeed despite a small timing mismatch. Optional collectibles can offer a harder route while the exit preserves forward progress. Our hypothesis is that a short retry loop makes this challenge easier to practice; test retry friction rather than assuming difficulty alone creates engagement.

## Art and audio study

The inspected draw path remaps hair slot 8: red with one dash, blue with none, and alternating white/bright green with two; it restores the mapping afterward. Hair is a five-part chain of filled circles following the player, so the sprite sheet alone does not capture the complete character. The psfx wrapper gates event sounds with sfx_timer. This links a resource state to both procedural art and event timing. Compare the silhouette against solid tiles and hazards at native resolution. Decode SFX notes and music patterns to study resource organization; a decoded note table is not a listening review. Examine feedback timing together with the relevant action, not as an isolated asset.

## Transfer experiment

Use recipe/spring-courier and pattern/forgiving-controls. Compare identical edge-jump and early-landing input traces with grace/buffering enabled and disabled. Record successful intended actions, accidental jumps, and time until the next attempt. Keep level geometry and speed fixed. Avoid copying the original character, levels or soundtrack.

Sources: https://www.lexaloffle.com/bbs/?tid=2145 and https://github.com/NoelFB/Celeste/blob/master/Source/PICO-8/Readme.md . The GitHub example is a C# port; the inspected artifact is the original PICO-8 cart. The BBS currently displays No License; this package distributes analysis and newly authored examples, not original assets.

case/just-one-boss.title: Just One Boss: readable attack phases
case/just-one-boss.content:
# Just One Boss: one input vocabulary, changing demands

Evidence: author-linked repository just_one_boss.p8, decoded locally; hashes and startup smoke are in research/inventory.json. No complete fight or subjective listening review has been performed for this case.

## Observed implementation

The author describes directional movement and collecting glowing tiles to defeat the boss while preserving hearts. The source distinguishes boss phases, sequences actions, and maps separate sounds to tile spawning, collection and player damage. Player injury sets invulnerability and stun durations. A reflection entity copies player motion with a transformed coordinate. Source anchors: decide_next_action, promise_sequence, player_reflection, spawn_magic_tile and get_hurt. These observations describe implementation, not a claim about the optimal strategy.

## Design interpretation

A stable control scheme leaves room for challenge to grow through spatial rules and timing. Moving toward an objective while avoiding attacks can create competing demands. Anticipation cues must make the upcoming danger legible before it becomes damaging; changes of phase should introduce a learnable variation. Avoid increasing speed, area and rule complexity simultaneously.

## Art and audio study

The magic-tile spawn draws expanding rectangle outlines before the collectible appears; the collectible remaps sprite color 7 to a cycling color. Source events assign SFX 8 on channel 3 to spawning, SFX 9 on channel 3 to collection, and SFX 17 on channel 0 to player hurt. These allocations describe this cart, not a channel layout to copy blindly. Compare anticipation, active and recovery poses rather than selecting attractive frames. The explicit spawn/collect/hurt sound triggers are useful event-to-feedback examples. Music changes at tutorial, fight and outcome transitions; extracting patterns alone does not establish that those transitions sound good.

## Transfer experiment

Use recipe/signal-arena and pattern/telegraph-attack-recovery. It is a newly authored lane-warning microgame, not a remake. Hold the warning duration fixed while changing the dangerous axis. Test whether a player can explain the next hit area before it fires. Test deliberately staying in danger, avoiding it and using the recovery opening.

Sources: https://aylanonsense.itch.io/just-one-boss and https://github.com/aylanonsense/just-one-boss . The author page labels the asset license CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Code and asset permissions must not be conflated. No third-party source or assets enter the model bundle.

# Porklike: turns as a decision budget

Evidence: original BBS porklike-2 cartridge decoded locally. Startup passes 120 frames; gameplay conclusions here are hypotheses grounded in source and author descriptions, not a completed run. See research/inventory.json for exact hashes.

## Observed implementation

The author describes a turn-based roguelike with nine floors, traps and enemies. Source passturn distinguishes player, AI and weeds phases. A noturn path can return to player handling without resolving the normal sequence. Animation update functions are separate from game-state updates. A step threshold triggers an additional threat. These are useful places to inspect which actions consume time, which are free, and how pressure limits indefinite waiting.

## Design interpretation

In turn-based games, consistent action costs are part of the controls. The player should understand whether movement, waiting, inventory actions and blocked moves give enemies a turn. An interesting route balances safety, resources and reward. A short deterministic authored map is a better first experiment than unverified procedural generation: establish meaningful choices before multiplying layouts.

## Art and audio study

The decoded sprite sheet uses nine slots: 0, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, 13 and 14. That is an asset statistic, not a limit on the runtime screen palette. The source indexes tile positions, visibility and animation separately. Pickup handling combines a floating text label with an event sound; a full inventory instead shows a rejection label and sound. A narrow resource palette still supports distinct item and action roles. Study whether known hazards, unexplored space and traversable floor remain distinct. Author credits identify Sebastian Hassler for music and separately permissioned inspirations for art. Trace event-triggered SFX and visibility feedback; do not treat every nonempty sprite or sound slot as an active game resource.

## Transfer experiment

Use recipe/lantern-vault, pattern/turn-economy and pattern/resource-pressure. It is an original fixed-map extraction puzzle. Test a direct escape route, optional detour, blocked movement, waiting and exhaustion. Compare success with remaining fuel, damage and optional reward. Confirm that leaving the game idle consumes no turns.

Sources: https://krystman.itch.io/porklike and https://www.lexaloffle.com/bbs/?pid=76877&tid=37045 . The author links a making-of tutorial; the release differs from the tutorial. The BBS displays No License. Original source/art/audio are local research material, not a reusable asset library.

case/high-stakes.title: High Stakes: information and optional risk
case/high-stakes.content:
# High Stakes: uncertainty with actionable information

Evidence: original highstakes-2 cartridge and author rules, with local decode and 120-frame startup verification. No complete match or listening review has been performed. Exact hashes are in research/inventory.json.

## Observed rules and implementation

The author describes a nine-card board with one losing card, rewards for revealing safe cards, information tokens unlocked by rows or columns, an option to identify the losing card directly, and a costly early exit. The source handles normal flipping, hint-token use, stabbing and passing separately. It also uses distinct SFX calls for accepted and rejected interactions. Source anchors: passcost, stabcard, flipbegin, dropchip functions and update_game.

## Design interpretation

Uncertainty becomes a decision when the player can use information or choose exposure. Always showing more rewards is insufficient if the next choice has no understandable consequence. Make the amount at risk, cost of exit and available information legible before commitment. Avoid inventing exact probabilities from an animation or assuming unknown cards are independent.

## Art and audio study

The input handler checks whether a hint token is valid for the selected card before consuming it. Accepted uses call SFX 60; rejected uses call SFX 61 and set curshake to 10. This is a concrete visual-plus-audio rejection response with no resource consumption. Study the hierarchy among hidden cards, revealed values, hint tokens and the current stakes display. Animations should confirm what changed without obscuring the next decision. The author credits Gruber Music. Compare confirm, reject and outcome sound roles; decoded sound data does not establish subjective quality.

## Transfer experiment

Read pattern/risk-reward and pattern/information-before-commitment. In recipe/lantern-vault, use an optional detour and visible fuel as an original deterministic alternative to random loss. Compare banked reward against successful extraction rate. A later card prototype should expose exact rules and use reproducible seeds for evaluation; do not reskin the original card artwork or copy its music.

Sources: https://krystman.itch.io/high-stakes and https://www.lexaloffle.com/bbs/?pid=83548 . The BBS labels this cartridge CC4-BY-NC-SA. This package retains provenance and analysis while keeping original assets outside the distributed model bundle.

pattern/forgiving-controls.title: Input forgiveness and consistent controls
pattern/forgiving-controls.content:
# Forgiving controls

These are transferable design proposals, not universal rules or copied implementations.

## Purpose

Make a deliberate action survive a small input-timing error. Useful for platforming; not a substitute for reachable geometry.

## Implementation

Track a brief jump buffer after a fresh press and a brief grace window after leaving ground. Consume both on a successful jump. Convert seconds to ticks at the actual update rate. Keep jump release behavior explicit.

## Tuning experiment

Starting experiment at 60 Hz: buffer 4 ticks, grace 5 ticks. These are our example parameters, not measured universal optima. Change one window at a time.

## Failure modes

Too-long windows create surprise jumps; stale buffers can jump after respawn. Clear them on reset. Do not let grace grant repeated midair jumps.

## Verification

Replay early press before landing, a late press after an edge, release/repress and continuous hold. Check failure outside the window as well as success inside it.

pattern/telegraph-attack-recovery.title: Readable attack phases
pattern/telegraph-attack-recovery.content:
# Telegraph, attack, recover

These are transferable design proposals, not universal rules or copied implementations.

## Purpose

Create an attack the player can anticipate, avoid and exploit.

## Implementation

Enter warning with a locked target. Show its future hit area. After a finite delay, activate exactly that area, then disable damage during recovery. Expose the vulnerable opportunity using shape/pose as well as color.

## Tuning experiment

In signal-arena, warning is 48/40/32 ticks across phases, active is 12, recovery is 60 at 60 Hz. Start long enough to teach; reduce only after a successful response.

## Failure modes

Tracking a player after the warning locks makes the cue misleading. Damage before the active state is unfair. A flash with no safe route is not a meaningful warning.

## Verification

Test staying in the lane, crossing during warning, leaving before activation and attacking during recovery. Assert the warning/active region does not change mid-cycle.

pattern/risk-reward.title: Optional risk and visible reward
pattern/risk-reward.content:
# Optional risk with a readable payoff

These are transferable design proposals, not universal rules or copied implementations.

## Purpose

Give the player a worthwhile optional commitment while preserving a clear main objective.

## Implementation

Provide a direct completion route and a detour with visible benefit and cost. State what can be lost. Bank reward at a distinct event; do not silently count unbanked loot as success.

## Tuning experiment

Vary detour length or reward independently. In lantern-vault optional gems add banked score but consume two extra fuel each; the player can choose routes avoiding them. Fuel and health limit collection.

## Failure modes

A reward on the only route is not optional. A dominated choice that is always worse is busywork. Hidden costs prevent informed decisions.

## Verification

Record completion rate, banked score and resource remainder for direct and greedy policies. Ask a human why they chose the detour; success metrics alone cannot establish enjoyment.

pattern/teach-vary-combine.title: Teach, vary, then combine
pattern/teach-vary-combine.content:
# Teach, vary, combine

These are transferable design proposals, not universal rules or copied implementations.

## Purpose

Introduce a mechanic in a safe context, then ask for a new application.

## Implementation

First show one rule with clear feedback. Change one spatial or timing variable. Combine only rules already demonstrated. Keep the input vocabulary stable while challenge changes.

## Tuning experiment

Use a three-beat sequence: forgiving first exposure, one variation, then a combination. Tune the first exposure separately from later difficulty.

## Failure modes

Changing enemy speed, range and controls at once makes failure hard to diagnose. Repeating the same room with more HP can add duration without new decisions.

## Verification

Ask a new player to describe the rule after the first encounter. Reuse an input trace to verify that the variation actually changes the challenge.

pattern/turn-economy.title: Action costs and turn resolution
pattern/turn-economy.content:
# Explicit turn economy

These are transferable design proposals, not universal rules or copied implementations.

## Purpose

Make action costs predictable in grid-based games.

## Implementation

Resolve input to one action, validate it, then commit world changes once. Decide whether blocked moves consume a turn. Keep animation clocks separate from simulation turns. Communicate wait as an intentional action.

## Tuning experiment

The vault charges one fuel for each valid move or wait. Each optional gem costs two additional fuel, stated above the board. Blocked moves and idle frames are free. A dangerous row resolves after the player action, then the next warning appears.

## Failure modes

Animation callbacks can accidentally run the enemy twice. Auto-repeat can spend several turns on one held key. Avoid ambiguous cancel or inventory costs.

## Verification

Check idle, wall bump, valid move, wait and fresh versus held input. Verify the same action list creates the same logical state regardless of idle frames inserted.

pattern/resource-pressure.title: Resources that change decisions
pattern/resource-pressure.content:
# Resources that create route decisions

These are transferable design proposals, not universal rules or copied implementations.

## Purpose

Limit an otherwise safe repeated action without making a new player fail before understanding it.

## Implementation

Choose a resource, a visible cost and a recovery/banking rule. Ensure the shortest valid route is affordable. Put optional value beyond that route. Show the resource before input is committed.

## Tuning experiment

Vault starts with 24 fuel. Measure path length including any waits demanded by hazards. Increase resource capacity if safe routes require unexplained precision.

## Failure modes

Resource exhaustion that arrives offscreen feels arbitrary. Refills on every safe loop can remove all pressure. A shortest path with zero slack can punish exploration excessively.

## Verification

Test an affordable direct route, a rewarding detour and deliberate exhaustion. Ensure win/loss precedence is explicit when arrival and the last resource expenditure coincide.

pattern/event-feedback.title: Coherent visual and audio event feedback
pattern/event-feedback.content:
# Coordinate art and audio around events

These are transferable design proposals, not universal rules or copied implementations.

## Purpose

Make important state transitions recognizable without overwhelming the playfield.

## Implementation

For each event choose a visual cue, sound cue and optional motion response. Prefer a distinct silhouette/pose and timing over color alone. Reserve channels so frequent SFX do not erase the music.

## Tuning experiment

Example layout: music on channel 0, feedback on 3. Use different pitch contours for pickup, hurt and success. Tune duration before increasing volume or shake.

## Failure modes

More particles can hide hazards. Loud repeating steps can mask damage. PCM activity confirms synthesis, not pleasantness; do not claim a listening review from RAM checks.

## Verification

Disable sound and verify critical states remain readable; inspect audio channel continuity and non-silent PCM. Have a human compare feedback intensity and perceived clarity.

pattern/information-before-commitment.title: Useful information before commitment
pattern/information-before-commitment.content:
# Information before commitment

These are transferable design proposals, not universal rules or copied implementations.

## Purpose

Allow the player to understand what is being risked before an irreversible action.

## Implementation

Show the current state, predicted consequence where deterministic, and cost of information where uncertain. Keep known and unknown facts visually distinct. A preview must use the same rules as execution.

## Tuning experiment

Begin with deterministic hazard previews. Add randomness only with a defined distribution and meaningful ways to respond.

## Failure modes

A flashing warning that differs from the actual hitbox teaches distrust. Invented probability labels mislead. Do not reveal hidden outcomes accidentally through UI or sound.

## Verification

Compare preview and outcome for every relevant state. Test whether a cautious and a risky policy yield distinguishable outcomes, and whether the player can explain the tradeoff.

recipe/spring-courier.content:
-- SPRING COURIER: carry the parcel to the gate; optional high gem.
-- New example code, pixel data and note sequences; no classic-game assets.
-- Resources: sprite 1 courier, sprite 2 gem; music SFX 0 / channel 0;
-- feedback SFX 1..4 / channel 3. All state is rebuilt by _init.
function assets()
 pal() palt()
 local art={
 {"000bb000","00b77b00","00bbbb00","000bb000","0bbbbbb0","000bb000","00b00b00","0bb00bb0"},
 {"000a0000","00aaa000","0aa7aa00","aa777aa0","0aaaaa00","00aaa000","000a0000","00000000"}}
 for n,rows in ipairs(art) do
  for y=0,7 do for x=0,7 do
   sset(n*8+x,y,tonum("0x"..sub(rows[y+1],x+1,x+1)))
  end end
 end
 for id=0,4 do
  local b=0x3200+id*68 memset(b,0,68)
  local notes=({{24,31,28,31,24,31,36,31},{36,40,43},{24,19,12},{36,43,48},{48,43,36}})[id+1]
  for i,k in ipairs(notes) do
   poke(b+(i-1)*2,k) poke(b+(i-1)*2+1,(id==0 and 2 or 5)*2)
  end
  poke(b+65,id==0 and 16 or 5)
  if id==0 then poke(b+66,0) poke(b+67,#notes) end
 end
 poke(0x3100,128,64,64,64) music(0,0,1)
end
function sound(id) sfx(id,3,0,id==0 and 8 or 3) end
function banner(title,subtitle)
 rectfill(5,39,122,85,1) rect(5,39,122,85,6)
 print(title,12,47,10) print(subtitle,12,59,7)
 print("x: start / retry",12,74,11)
end

-- Arrows move, O/Z jumps. X starts or retries. 60 Hz.
-- Tune speed, jump_v, gravity together; windows are update ticks.
speed=1.2 jump_v=-3.5 gravity=0.18 grace_ticks=5 buffer_ticks=4
function _init()
 assets() state="title" px=8 py=100 vy=0 grace=0 buffer=0
 parcel=false bonus=false ticks=0
 floors={{0,108,40,20},{56,108,28,20},{100,108,28,20},{58,88,22,4}}
end
function start()
 state="play" px=8 py=100 vy=0 grace=0 buffer=0
 parcel=false bonus=false ticks=0
end
function standing()
 for f in all(floors) do
  if px+6>f[1] and px<f[1]+f[3] and abs(py+8-f[2])<0.05 then return true end
 end
 return false
end
function _update60()
 ticks+=1
 if state!="play" then
  if btnp(5) then start() end
  return
 end
 if standing() then grace=grace_ticks else grace=max(0,grace-1) end
 if btnp(4) then buffer=buffer_ticks else buffer=max(0,buffer-1) end
 if buffer>0 and grace>0 then

 local dx,dy=0,0
 if btnp(0) then dx=-1 elseif btnp(1) then dx=1
 elseif btnp(2) then dy=-1 elseif btnp(3) then dy=1 end
 local wait=btnp(4)
 if dx==0 and dy==0 and not wait then return end
 if blocked(tx+dx,ty+dy) then sound(4) return end
 tx+=dx ty+=dy fuel-=1 turn+=1
 if ty==danger then hp-=1 flash=20 sound(2) end
 danger=turn%5+1
 if tx==5 and ty==1 and not relic then relic=true sound(1) end
 for i,g in ipairs(gem_cells) do
  if tx==g[1] and ty==g[2] and not taken[i] then
   taken[i]=true gems+=1 fuel-=2 sound(1)
  end
 end
 if hp<=0 then state="lost"
 elseif tx==1 and ty==5 and relic then state="won" sound(3)
 elseif fuel<=0 then state="lost" sound(2) end
end
function _draw()
 cls(1)
 print("lantern vault",4,3,7)
 print("fuel:"..fuel.." hp:"..hp,4,11,11)
 print("pink gem: -2 fuel",4,19,14)
 for y=1,5 do for x=1,5 do
  local sx,sy=8+x*18,10+y*18
  rectfill(sx,sy,sx+15,sy+15,blocked(x,y) and 5 or 2)
  if y==danger and not blocked(x,y) then
   rect(sx,sy,sx+15,sy+15,9) print("!",sx+1,sy+1,9)
  end
 end end
 rect(26,100,41,115,11)
 if not relic then spr(2,101,32) end
 for i,g in ipairs(gem_cells) do
  if not taken[i] then circ(15+g[1]*18,17+g[2]*18,3,14) end
 end
 if flash%6<3 then spr(1,12+tx*18,14+ty*18) end
 print(relic and "return to green pad" or "relic: top right",4,120,7)
 if state=="title" then banner("lantern vault","arrows move / o wait") end
 if state=="lost" then banner("lantern faded","row ! hurts next turn") end
 if state=="won" then banner("relic recovered!","banked gems: "..gems) end
end
